request.system: You assist requirements analysts who apply the OGORE framework. You refine one IT goal of an organization's Initial Goal Tree Model by adapting validated goal patterns retrieved from a Goal Knowledge Base. Use only the six OGORE element types: Goal, Task, Resource, Actor, Belief, Constraint. Do not invent KPI values.

messages.content:
RETRIEVED PATTERNS:
[SKB-01/G2] (similarity 0.5677)
PATTERN SKB-01 | medium-sized food and beverage distributor (synthetic) | wholesale distribution; order-to-cash and lot traceability
Organization goal: deliver complete and traceable orders to retail customers
IT goal G2: Customer orders recorded accurately (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Order lines matching the customer purchase order (target 99.5%); G2-K2 Order confirmation sent after entry (target within 30 minutes)
  Tasks: Capture customer purchase order with price list validation; Confirm order to customer
  Resources: Customer price list; Order management module
  Actors: Sales Administrator; Customer
  Beliefs: Price lists are customer specific
  Constraints: A confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request
  Conflict resolved: lot scanning slows picking and delays confirmation -> confirm the order at entry and scan lots at picking, so confirmation time is unaffected

[SKB-07/G2] (similarity 0.5332)
PATTERN SKB-07 | hospital pharmacy (synthetic) | medicine handling; expiry and dispensing control
Organization goal: dispense safe medicines without waste from expiry
IT goal G2: Expiry dates controlled (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G2-K1 Items picked first-expiry-first-out (target 100%); G2-K2 Expired items removed from stock (target within 1 day of expiry)
  Tasks: Record batch and expiry at receipt; Suggest picking by earliest expiry; Report items expiring within 90 days
  Resources: Pharmacy stock module
  Actors: Pharmacist in Charge; Pharmacy Technician
  Beliefs: Regulation requires batch records for every medicine
  Constraints: Only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines
  Rational statement: Batch and expiry captured at receipt make both FEFO picking and recalls possible.

[SKB-01/G3] (similarity 0.4656)
PATTERN SKB-01 | medium-sized food and beverage distributor (synthetic) | wholesale distribution; order-to-cash and lot traceability
Organization goal: deliver complete and traceable orders to retail customers
IT goal G3: Lot numbers traceable from receipt to customer (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G3-K1 Shipped lines with lot number recorded (target 100%); G3-K2 Time to list all customers of a recalled lot (target under 4 hours)
  Tasks: Scan lot number at goods receipt; Record lot number on each picked line; Run recall trace report
  Resources: Barcode scanners; Lot master data
  Actors: Warehouse Clerk; Quality Officer
  Beliefs: Suppliers print lot numbers on every carton
  Constraints: A line without a lot number cannot be shipped
  Rational statement: Lot capture at receipt and picking makes a recall trace a query instead of a manual search, which is what the 4-hour KPI requires.
  Conflict resolved: lot scanning slows picking and delays confirmation -> confirm the order at entry and scan lots at picking, so confirmation time is unaffected

[SKB-05/G3] (similarity 0.4489)
PATTERN SKB-05 | insurance company (synthetic) | customer service; governance of an LLM-based assistant with retrieval
Organization goal: offer fast, correct, and accountable answers to customers
IT goal G3: AI risks governed (parent G1, AND)
  KPIs: G3-K1 Model or prompt changes recorded and approved before release (target 100%); G3-K2 Risk assessment of the assistant reviewed (target every 6 months)
  Tasks: Keep a model and prompt change register; Review the AI risk assessment with the risk committee
  Resources: Change register; AI risk register
  Actors: AI Product Owner; Risk Officer
  Beliefs: none
  Constraints: Customer personal data is not sent to the model provider beyond the session
  Rational statement: A change register makes every model or prompt change attributable, which the evaluation KPI depends on.

QUERY:
GOAL: G02 "Hospital orders recorded accurately and confirmed promptly"; parent G01 "Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure"
DOMAIN: pharmaceutical distribution to hospitals; organization type: medium-sized distributor with an order portal and an LLM-based ordering assistant
KPIS: G02-K1 = Order lines matching the hospital purchase order (>= 99.5% per month); G02-K2 = Order confirmation sent after submission (within 15 minutes)
ACTORS IN SCOPE: Hospital Buyer; Sales Administrator; Responsible Pharmacist; Quality Assurance Officer; IT Security Officer; Data Protection Officer; AI Product Owner
BELIEFS: Each hospital has a contract price list; Hospital buyers order through the portal or the assistant
CONSTRAINTS: A confirmed order cannot be changed without a change request

TASK: (1) Rank the retrieved patterns by relevance to the query and state why each is relevant, citing its pattern ID. (2) Adapt them to the query and propose Tasks, Actors, Resources, Beliefs, and Constraints for the goal (and sub-goals only if the goal needs further decomposition). (3) Link every proposed element to the goal ID or to one of its KPI IDs, exactly as given in the query. (4) Draft one rational statement that explains how the goal and its elements serve the parent goal and its KPIs. (5) Give, for each element, the pattern ID it was adapted from; if it was not taken from a retrieved pattern, write UNGROUNDED. Every proposed element must respect the beliefs and constraints listed in the query.

ranked_patterns.relevance: Highest relevance: SKB-01/G2 is the same IT goal type (customer orders recorded accurately) with the same two KPI shapes as G02 (order lines matching the purchase order at 99.5%; confirmation sent after entry within a time window), the same contract/customer-specific price list belief, and the identical constraint that a confirmed order cannot be edited without a change request. Its conflict resolution (confirm at entry, do traceability work later in the flow) transfers directly to the tighter 15-minute confirmation KPI G02-K2.

Second: SKB-05/G3 governs an LLM assistant with retrieval in a customer-facing ordering/answering context, which matches the query organization's LLM-based ordering assistant, the AI Product Owner actor, and the data-protection scope (Data Protection Officer, IT Security Officer). Its change register and 'no customer personal data to the model provider beyond the session' constraint are reusable to keep assistant-created order lines accurate and attributable for G02-K1.

Third: SKB-01/G3 comes from the same distribution pattern and the same parent organization goal (complete and traceable orders). It contributes the blocking-constraint style ('a line without X cannot be shipped') and the receipt/entry data-capture discipline, which is adapted here as 'a line without a valid contract price or catalogue match cannot be confirmed' supporting G02-K1; its lot traceability tasks themselves belong to a sibling goal, not to G02.

Fourth: SKB-07/G2 is a pharmacy/medicines pattern and supplies the regulated-product context of the query (Responsible Pharmacist role, pharmacist-only release of restricted items, regulatory record keeping). It is less relevant to order recording accuracy itself because its KPIs concern expiry and FEFO picking, but its actor and release constraint are adapted so that regulatory checks do not delay the 15-minute confirmation.

elements.text: Capture the hospital purchase order (portal, assistant or manual entry) and validate every line automatically against the hospital contract price list and the product catalogue
elements.justification: Direct adaptation of 'Capture customer purchase order with price list validation'; validation at entry is what makes order lines match the hospital purchase order at the 99.5% target, and it respects the belief that each hospital has a contract price list.

elements.text: Send the order confirmation to the hospital buyer automatically on submission, before any downstream regulatory or lot checks are performed
elements.justification: Adapts 'Confirm order to customer' together with the pattern's resolved conflict (confirm at entry, scan lots at picking) so that the tighter 15-minute confirmation window is not consumed by pharmacist or traceability checks.

elements.text: Require the hospital buyer to review and accept assistant-proposed order lines before the order is submitted, and record the accepted lines with their source channel
elements.justification: Adapts the governance idea that assistant output must be attributable and approved; it protects the line-matching KPI when orders arrive through the LLM assistant, consistent with the belief that buyers order through the portal or the assistant.

elements.text: Maintain a model and prompt change register for the ordering assistant and approve each change before release
elements.justification: Taken from 'Keep a model and prompt change register'; uncontrolled prompt or model changes are the main way assistant-entered lines start deviating from the hospital purchase order, so the register defends G02-K1.

elements.text: Process every requested change to a confirmed order as a formal change request with a new confirmation to the hospital buyer
elements.justification: Operationalizes the query constraint on confirmed orders and keeps the recorded order identical to the agreed hospital purchase order.

elements.text: Measure and report monthly the order line match rate and the submission-to-confirmation time by channel (portal, assistant, manual)
elements.justification: Adapts the periodic review discipline of the AI governance pattern to produce the evidence for both G02 KPIs and to expose any channel where the 15-minute target is missed.

elements.text: Hospital Buyer
elements.justification: Plays the 'Customer' role of the pattern: issues the purchase order and accepts assistant-proposed lines, which is the reference against which line matching is measured.

elements.text: Sales Administrator
elements.justification: Same actor as in the pattern; owns manual order entry, price list validation exceptions and change requests on confirmed orders.

elements.text: AI Product Owner
elements.justification: Pattern actor responsible for the assistant's change register and release approval, hence accountable for the accuracy of assistant-entered order lines.

elements.text: Data Protection Officer
elements.justification: Adapted from the Risk Officer role; oversees that order data handled by the portal and the assistant stays within the session and provider limits while the order is recorded.

elements.text: Responsible Pharmacist
elements.justification: Adapts 'Pharmacist in Charge'; releases order lines for restricted medicines after confirmation, so the regulated check is covered without blocking the confirmation KPI.

elements.text: Hospital contract price list
elements.justification: Adaptation of 'Customer price list' to the query belief that each hospital has a contract price list; it is the reference data for line and price validation.

elements.text: Order management module with hospital ordering portal
elements.justification: Adaptation of 'Order management module'; it records the submitted order and issues the automatic confirmation that the 15-minute KPI measures.

elements.text: LLM ordering assistant with retrieval over the contract price list and product catalogue
elements.justification: The retrieval-grounded assistant of the pattern, adapted to ordering: grounding proposals in contract and catalogue data keeps assistant-created lines aligned with the hospital purchase order.

elements.text: Model and prompt change register for the ordering assistant
elements.justification: Pattern resource 'Change register'; makes every assistant behaviour change attributable when line-matching deviations are investigated.

elements.text: Order audit trail recording entry channel, user, timestamp and confirmation time
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern's capture-at-source traceability data so that confirmation timing and order content become a query rather than a manual reconstruction.

elements.text: Each hospital has a contract price list, so prices and allowed products are customer specific
elements.justification: Pattern belief 'Price lists are customer specific' restated with the query belief; it justifies validating every line against a hospital-specific contract.

elements.text: Hospital buyers order through the portal or through the LLM assistant, so accuracy controls must cover both channels
elements.justification: Stated in the query; no retrieved pattern covers multi-channel order entry, so it is carried over unchanged to scope the controls.

elements.text: Regulation requires an auditable record of every medicine order line and of who entered or approved it
elements.justification: Adapts 'Regulation requires batch records for every medicine' to the order-recording goal of a pharmaceutical distributor serving hospitals.

elements.text: A confirmed order cannot be changed without an approved change request
elements.justification: Identical constraint in the query and in the pattern; it keeps the recorded order stable so the monthly line-matching measurement remains meaningful.

elements.text: An order line without a valid contract price and a matching catalogue product cannot be confirmed
elements.justification: Adapts the blocking rule 'a line without a lot number cannot be shipped' to order entry, making the 99.5% line-matching target enforceable by the system rather than by inspection.

elements.text: Order lines proposed by the LLM assistant are only recorded after explicit acceptance by the hospital buyer
elements.justification: Adapts the pattern's accountability requirement for model output to the ordering case, preventing unverified assistant content from entering the order record.

elements.text: Hospital and buyer personal data is not sent to the model provider beyond the session
elements.justification: Pattern constraint reused unchanged; it bounds how the assistant may process order data while still supporting accurate, prompt order capture.

elements.text: Only the Responsible Pharmacist may release confirmed order lines for restricted or controlled medicines, and this release is performed after confirmation
elements.justification: Adapts 'Only a pharmacist may release quarantined medicines' and applies the SKB-01 conflict resolution so the regulatory release does not consume the 15-minute confirmation window.

output.rational_statement: G02 serves the parent goal G01 'Regulated order-to-delivery controlled and secure' because a delivery can only be regulated, controlled and secure if the order it is based on is an accurate and attributable record of what the hospital actually ordered: validating every line against the hospital contract price list and catalogue at entry, blocking lines without a valid contract price, and requiring explicit buyer acceptance of assistant-proposed lines make the 99.5% line-matching target of G02-K1 a system-enforced property across the portal, assistant and manual channels, while the change register and order audit trail make every assistant change and every recorded line attributable for regulatory and security review. The 15-minute confirmation target of G02-K2 is protected by applying the SKB-01 conflict resolution to this context: the order management module confirms automatically at submission, whereas the Responsible Pharmacist's release of restricted medicines and the downstream lot and delivery controls occur after confirmation, so regulatory rigour is added to the order-to-delivery chain without delaying the customer commitment; the change-request constraint on confirmed orders, the pharmacist-only release and the no-personal-data-to-the-provider constraint then keep the recorded order stable, compliant and secure as it flows into the sibling goals of G01. No further decomposition of G02 is needed, since all proposed elements attach directly to G02, G02-K1 or G02-K2.
